original_value: Several mathematical frameworks have been used to model the information retrieval (IR) process, among them, formal logics. Logic-based IR models upgrade the IR process from document-query comparison to an inference process, in which both documents and queries are expressed as sentences of the selected formal logic. The underlying formal logic also permits one to represent and integrate knowledge in the IR process. One of the main obstacles that has prevented the adoption and large-scale diffusion of logic-based IR systems is their complexity. However, several logic-based IR models have been recently proposed that are applicable to large-scale data collections. In this survey, we present an overview of the most prominent logical IR models that have been proposed in the literature. The considered logical models are categorized under different axes, which include the considered logics and the way in which uncertainty has been modeled, for example, degrees of belief or degrees of truth. Accordingly, the main contribution of the article is to categorize the state-of-the-art logical models on a fine-grained basis, and for the considered models the related implementation aspects are described. Consequently, the proposed survey is finalized to better understand and compare the different logical IR models. Last, but not least, this article aims at reconsidering the potentials of logical approaches to IR by outlining the advances of logic-based approaches in close research areas.

result.paraphrase: Various mathematical frameworks, including formal logics, have been applied to model the information retrieval (IR) process. In logic-based IR, retrieval is recast as an inference task rather than a document-query comparison, with both documents and queries represented as sentences in the chosen formal logic. Such logics also make it possible to represent and incorporate knowledge into IR. A key barrier to the adoption and widespread dissemination of logic-based IR systems has been their complexity. Even so, several logic-based IR models suited to large-scale data collections have recently been introduced. This survey provides an overview of the most prominent logical IR models in the literature. The models are organized along several dimensions, including the logic employed and how uncertainty is represented, such as by degrees of belief or degrees of truth. The article’s main contribution is a fine-grained classification of the state of the art in logical models, along with descriptions of the implementation aspects of the models considered. As a result, the survey is intended to improve understanding of and comparison between the various logical IR models. Finally, it also seeks to reassess the potential of logical approaches to IR by highlighting progress in closely related research areas.
